rows.label: Concept
rows.text: An emf is induced only while flux linkage is changing, and its magnitude is N times the rate of change of flux. More turns or a faster change mean a larger emf. A steady flux induces nothing, and Lenz's law fixes the direction.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
F = qvB sinθ
ε = −N dΦ/dt
F = BIL

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: 1 V = 1 Wb/s.  ·  A search coil measures a changing field by the induced emf.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Faraday found that an emf appears in a coil while the magnetic flux through it is changing. A bar magnet at rest in the coil, however strong, induces nothing.  ·  The flux through one turn is B times the perpendicular area. For N turns the flux linkage is N times that flux. The induced emf equals the negative of the rate of change of flux linkage.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Flux linkage  ·  Faraday emf  ·  Many turns  ·  Open-circuit emf

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: • Faraday's laws of electromagnetic induction  ·  A changing flux induces an emf.  ·  More turns mean a larger emf.  ·  A steady flux induces nothing.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Force on moving charge F = q(v×B); on a wire F = BIL sinθ.  ·  Faraday: EMF ε = −dΦ/dt; Lenz's law gives the sign (induced current opposes the change in flux).

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: What does the minus sign mean?

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: A coil of 100 turns has its flux increased by 0.020 Wb in 0.50 s. Find the magnitude of the average induced emf.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: A magnet at rest in a coil induces → B  ·  The induced emf is larger when → A

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: The flux can be changed by moving the magnet, by switching the field, by changing the area of the loop, or by rotating the coil. A generator uses the rotation.  ·  A faster change produces a larger emf. Doubling N doubles the emf for the same change of flux per turn. That is why a search coil has many turns.  ·  If the circuit is closed, the emf drives an induced current. If the circuit is open, the emf is still there and can be read by a voltmeter, but no current flows.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: L = NΦ/I  ·  The minus sign is Lenz's law.  ·  ❌ skip the key fact → ✅ force on moving charge f = q(v×b); on a wire f = bil sinθ..

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: A steady field does not induce an emf.  ·  The emf depends on the rate, not on the flux alone.  ·  N multiplies the emf.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: An open circuit can have an emf and no current.  ·  Include N when the coil has many turns.  ·  Say what is changing.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Write Induced emf = − N dΦ/dt and say what each symbol means.  ·  Mark the known values, then substitute one step at a time.  ·  Finish with the number, the unit, and the direction when the quantity has one.

rows.text: Self-inductance L = NΦ/I; inductance stores energy U = ½LI². Mutual inductance M couples two coils.  ·  State the limit / condition where a formula or rule stops being valid before applying it.  ·  Limit to remember: force on moving charge f = q(v×b); on a wire f = bil sinθ.
